head: eaabbe8cd3b4e96426c3ccb67f01d603479d452f
summary:
This review covered attempt 4 (ae20467..eaabbe8) and what it reaches. The build had 0 warnings, the default suite passed 119/119 and CancelledFolderTests passed 6/6. Fitness reports all 14 rules hold. I rebuilt the builder's O-031 harness in a temp folder of my own, ran it against the built App's MainWindow.UnlessCancelled, and it passed 4/4:
- Cancel before the query: the query never started.
- Cancel during a blocked query: the wait ended 2.3 ms after Cancel while the query was still running.
- No Cancel: the result came back.
- The query ran on its own thread.

I then removed the temp folder.

**O-031.** MainWindow now runs only Scanner.Scan on the LongRunning thread. VolumeInUse goes through UnlessCancelled, which returns null at once if Cancel was already requested. Otherwise it runs the query on its own thread and awaits it with WaitAsync(token). Both cases the disposition names are covered.

**O-032.** LastCallAborted is set true when Enter refuses a call, and set to `issued` by Exit. DirectoryReader.List resets only when LastCallAborted is true. The two new tests feed a 995 with no cancel requested through the real reader and the real scanner, and they discriminate: 'reset on any 995' fails them, and never resetting fails the abort test.

**What the moved behaviour made false.** Every Stopped ending is a scan whose token was already cancelled when Scan returned; Scanner can only return Cancelled under a requested cancel. So UnlessCancelled now returns null for every Stopped ending. That has two consequences:
- The design doc's 'Finished and Stopped also show the volume's used space' is false.
- MainWindow.Coverage's partial-scan branch is dead.

**A retention issue.** The orphaned query's closure holds the whole ScanResult. On a mapped drive that stopped answering, that keeps the previous scan's store alive, which line 123 explicitly tries to release.

Both findings are minor.

findings.claim: The new code means a Stopped ending never shows the volume line. The design doc still says it does, and MainWindow keeps an unreachable branch for it. ScanStatus.Cancelled is returned only under a requested cancel: Scanner.Execute line 73, ClassifyReadError requiring cancelRequested, and FolderDone's `return ct.IsCancellationRequested`. So by the time StartScan calls UnlessCancelled for a Stopped scan, `token.IsCancellationRequested` is already true and the call returns null without querying. The doc (docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:45-47) still says 'Finished and Stopped also show the volume's used space ... (O-013)', and the added sentence only says a cancelled scan omits it. A reader cannot tell that the Stopped half of O-013 is gone for good. The M1 disposition asked for the doc to say a cancelled scan 'may omit' the line; the truth is that it always does. Coverage(finished: false, ...) at MainWindow.xaml.cs:296-299, the 'not in this partial scan' text, can no longer run. The build did not declare either consequence.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:148 `volumeInUse = await UnlessCancelled(() => VolumeInUse(scan), token);` and :187-188 `if (token.IsCancellationRequested) return null;`. Coverage at :261 is called only when volumeInUse is a long, and :299 is the partial branch. Scanner.cs:73, 79, 139, 165 are the only ways to reach Cancelled. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:45-48.
findings.fix: Change docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:45-47 to say that only Finished shows the volume line and that Stopped never does since SL-024 (O-031), because the query is not started once Cancel was requested. Then either delete Coverage's `finished` parameter and the partial-scan branch, or keep the branch with a comment saying why it cannot run today.

findings.claim: UnlessCancelled's orphaned query captures the whole ScanResult (`() => VolumeInUse(scan)`), so the scan's ScanStore stays reachable until GetDiskFreeSpaceEx returns. The case this code exists for is a mapped drive that stopped answering, where that is up to the SMB client's limit (62-66 s measured in build 3). On that drive a person can cancel the wait and start a new scan straight away: the pickers are re-enabled in `finally`, and StartScan sets `_result = null; // let the previous scan's store be collected` (line 123). The old store cannot be collected while the orphaned query holds it, so two stores are live together. U-001 measured one 5M-entry scan at 699 MiB peak against the 1 GB budget.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:147-148 `ScanResult scan = result; volumeInUse = await UnlessCancelled(() => VolumeInUse(scan), token);` and :123. VolumeInUse (:202-207) reads only scan.Root and scan.Status.
findings.fix: Capture only what the query needs. Change VolumeInUse to take `(string root, ScanStatus status)`, or compute `string root = result.Root; bool query = result.Status != ScanStatus.RootUnreadable;` before the call, and pass `() => VolumeInUse(root, query)`. The orphaned thread then holds two small values instead of the store.

obligations.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:145-148 has the scan thread running only Scanner.Scan. UnlessCancelled (:185-198) returns null when the token is already cancelled. Otherwise it starts VolumeInUse as a LongRunning task and awaits `running.WaitAsync(token)`, catching OperationCanceledException only when the token was cancelled. I rebuilt and ran the harness (.taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-4-o031/Program.cs) against the built App dll and it passed 4/4. The doc edit is only partly right; see m1.

In SynchronousIoCancel.cs, LastCallAborted is set true in Enter's refusal branch and assigned `issued` in Exit. DirectoryReader.List resets `_count`/`_namesUsed` only `if (io.LastCallAborted)`. CancelledFolderTests.A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelKeepsWhatWasListed covers the reader: Count is between 1 and 1999, LastCallAborted is false and ClosesHandedOff is 0. A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelIsAnUnreadableFolderAndTheScanCarriesOn covers the scanner: status Completed, a single Unreadable(995) with partial children, and z committed. AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt now asserts LastCallAborted. I ran all of them and they passed.

This attempt did not change it. Enter still refuses after cancel and Dispose still joins the canceller (SynchronousIoCancel.cs). The new LastCallAborted assignment in Enter's refusal branch does not change the refusal. NoCallStartsOnceCancelIsRequested and the stress test pass in the 119/119 run.

This attempt did not change it. The token callback still only starts scan-cancel. On the App side, UnlessCancelled adds a WaitAsync registration on the token, which completes a task and does no I/O on the UI thread; the harness measured the wait ending 2.3 ms after Cancel.

This attempt did not change it. SynchronousIoCancel.Close still hands aborted handles to the pool. The new test asserts that a 995 Windows returns without a cancel is closed inline (ClosesHandedOff 0), which is correct because nothing was aborted.

drift: O-031 has no test in the repository. Its only executable proof is the untracked harness in .taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-4-o031, which reaches the private MainWindow.UnlessCancelled by reflection. That follows the recorded decision to have no App test project, but a rename or signature change to UnlessCancelled breaks nothing in the suite.

If Cancel arrives while a completed scan's volume query is blocked, the window goes from 'Stopping...' to a 'Finished' ending with no volume line. The scan did finish, so this is correct, but neither the doc nor the build account describes this ending.

A completed, uncancelled scan of a mapped drive that stopped answering still waits for GetDiskFreeSpaceEx, up to the SMB client's limit. Cancel ends that wait. This was declared as a follow-up, and skipping the query for DriveType.Network roots is left as a product choice.

cases.evidence: It now goes beyond the pure ClassifyReadError theory. CancelledFolderTests.A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelIsAnUnreadableFolderAndTheScanCarriesOn uses a live token that is never cancelled, and OverrideQueryError returns 995 at big's third listing buffer through the real Scanner. The scan is Completed, big is a single Unreadable(995) with 1-1999 children, and z is committed. A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelKeepsWhatWasListed feeds the same shape at reader level.

It is unchanged, and AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt now also asserts `guard.LastCallAborted` after an abort at the third buffer, in both the before-call and during-call modes. The CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders sweep still passes.

unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-024/build-slice-4-o031/README.md and readwindow-D.txt: evidence files. I read and re-ran the harness (Program.cs, o031.csproj) and read o031.log, but did not open these two.
